extracted.intended_audience: approved nominating organisations, organisations wishing to become nominators, and others interested in the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award selection process
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural rules for nominating and selecting the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award laureate, including eligibility, core evaluative standards, timeline, and how organisations become nominators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible laureates (roles/types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laureates shall be authors, illustrators, storytellers or reading promoters; the Award is also given to people or organizations that work to promote reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutes specify the types of persons/organisations eligible: creators (authors, illustrators, storytellers) and reading promoters/organisations whose work promotes reading for children and young adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience (children and young adults)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work or activity considered must be for children and young adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and evaluation focus specifically on contributions aimed at children and young adult audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Work or activity must be "of the highest artistic quality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core statutory standard from the Award's statutes and functions as a primary evaluative criterion for the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanistic spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Work or activity must "convey the deeply humanistic spirit associated with Astrid Lindgren."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutes require that laureates embody this particular humanistic spirit; the site links to additional explanation of what that spirit means for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination eligibility & procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only approved nominating organisations may submit nominations; the invitation specifies the number of candidates and categories each body can suggest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline and procedural rules: nominations open in January; all information must reach the award office by the announced (May) deadline; late or incomplete nominations will not be accepted. The list of nominated candidates is usually presented in October (Frankfurt Book Fair) and published on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming a nominator (application requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisations wishing to become nominating bodies must apply before December 1 by emailing nomination@alma.se with a brief description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jury decides on the list of nominating bodies in December; if accepted, the organisation is eligible to submit nominations for the following year after nominations open in January.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury expertise & evaluation capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The twelve-member expert jury must have extensive knowledge of international children’s and YA literature as well as children's rights and children's reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasizes that "rewarding the highest-quality work demands an expert knowledge" in these areas; the jury evaluates prominent international candidates and selects the laureate accordingly.
